final_answer.conclusion: Holiday Sale produced more total completed-order merchandise gross profit, while Black Friday produced more merchandise gross profit per promotion day because it ran for fewer days.
final_answer.recommended_next_step: Investigate incremental demand, cannibalization, customer mix, and costs not represented in merchandise cost before choosing which promotion to repeat.
supporting_facts: Holiday Sale produced $67,286.45 in merchandise gross profit versus $30,445.47 for Black Friday.
Black Friday produced $4,349.35 per promotion day versus $3,958.03 for Holiday Sale.
final_answer.important_limitation: This descriptive comparison does not establish incremental profit or causation.

methodology.population: Completed NovaMart orders associated with Black Friday or Holiday Sale.
methodology.grain: One output row per promotion after calculating merchandise gross profit at the item level.
methodology.calculation_summary: Sum line_total minus quantity multiplied by product cost, then divide by inclusive promotion days.
validation_checks: Counted distinct orders after the item-level join.
Reconciled discounted merchandise value to order subtotal less order discount.
assumptions: Product cost is the available merchandise cost and excludes marketing, shipping, and other company costs.
